notes: Only the six advertised tools were labelled. The experimental tools referenced by the server (`build`, `test`, `e2e`, `modernize`, `devserver.*`) execute `ng` through `host.runCommand` and would be HOSTEXEC, but they are not advertised by default (mcp-server.js:54-60, 171-182).

`onpush_zoneless_migration` takes a raw absolute path and is not routed through `resolveWorkspaceAndProject`'s root check (workspace-utils.js:101-105), so its file reads are not confined to the MCP roots based on the code shown.

`search_documentation` decrypts a search-only Algolia key at runtime (doc-search.js:146-148) and always queries the same vendor app/index, so it is not an agent-chosen destination; the optional page fetch is hostname-pinned to angular.dev (doc-search.js:194).

`get_best_practices` and `find_examples` both accept an arbitrary `workspacePath`; the best-practices path is bounded by a package-boundary traversal check, while the examples path resolution lives in the unprovided `database-discovery` module.

ai_tutor.rationale: `AI_TUTOR_TOOL` only reads a static markdown resource shipped inside the CLI package (`../resources/ai-tutor.md`) and returns it. No user data, no network egress, no execution. The content is package-bundled and therefore public, so it is neither SECRET nor attacker-controllable.

find_examples.rationale: The handler opens SQLite files on the host and returns rows into the agent context: the bundled `exampleDatabasePath`, databases discovered from the caller-supplied `input.workspacePath` via `getVersionSpecificExampleDatabases`, or an arbitrary directory named by `NG_MCP_EXAMPLES_DIR` through `setupRuntimeExamples`. The discovery module (`./database-discovery`) and `queryDatabase`/`validateDatabaseSchema` implementations are not in the provided source, so which host paths can be opened and how much of their content is echoed is not settled; keeping SECRET for local database content read with the user's filesystem access. No network egress or command execution in this file.

get_best_practices.rationale: `createBestPracticesHandler` either returns the CLI-bundled `best-practices.md` (`getBundledBestPractices`) or a markdown file referenced by `angular.bestPractices.path` inside the resolved `@angular/core` package. The read is pinned to the installed package directory: `relative`/`isAbsolute` traversal check plus a 1MB size cap (best-practices.js:118-131), so it cannot exfiltrate arbitrary user files; the returned bytes are published npm package content, not private data. No network sink, no command execution.

list_projects.rationale: `createListProjectsHandler` walks the client roots (or `process.cwd()` when the client has no roots capability, projects.js:461-467) with `findAngularJsonFiles`, loads every `angular.json` via `AngularWorkspace.load`, and returns local paths, project names, builders, source roots and `@angular/core` versions (`findAngularCoreVersion` reads local `package.json` files, projects.js:246). This is private host/workspace data surfaced into the agent context. It does not send data anywhere and does not execute commands.

onpush_zoneless_migration.rationale: `fileOrDirPath` is an unconstrained absolute path: `statSync` then `glob(`${fileOrDirPath}/**/*.ts`)` enumerates the tree and `createSourceFile` reads each file's full text (`sourceFile.getFullText()`, line 156). Results flow back through `analyzeForUnsupportedZoneUses`, `migrateSingleFile`, `migrateTestFile` and `createResponse`, plus error text containing discovered file paths (line 99), so private local source is reachable in the agent context. There is no workspace-root restriction here (unlike `resolveWorkspaceAndProject`). `rankComponentFilesForMigration` only sends file names back to the MCP client via `sampling/createMessage` (line 182), which is the user's own client, not an attacker-readable destination, so no SINK. The helper modules (`prompts`, `migrate-single-file`, `ts-utils`) are not provided, so exactly how much file content is echoed is undetermined; SECRET is kept.

search_documentation.rationale: The handler sends `query` only to the fixed Algolia application `ALGOLIA_APP_ID` index `angular_v<version>` (doc-search.js:298-322), which is a fixed vendor endpoint and therefore not a SINK; the agent cannot choose the destination. Content fetching is gated on `url.hostname === 'angular.dev' || url.hostname.endsWith('.angular.dev')` before `fetch` (doc-search.js:194-196), so returned page text comes from the Angular vendor site rather than attacker-controlled hosts; `extractMainContent` only keeps `<main>` text. No local file or credentialed data is returned.

value_conditions.default: off - all stable tools including search_documentation are advertised
value_conditions.effect: Filters the advertised set to tools with `isLocalOnly === true`, which removes `search_documentation` (the only tool with `isLocalOnly: false`) and hence removes the outbound Algolia/angular.dev network access.

Filters to tools with `isReadOnly === true`. All six advertised tools are read-only, so labels are unchanged; it does prevent the experimental write/exec tools (`build`, `modernize`) from being added.

value_conditions.default: empty - none of the experimental tools are advertised
value_conditions.effect: Adds EXPERIMENTAL_TOOLS such as `build` and `modernize`, which invoke `context.host.runCommand('ng', args, {cwd})` and would be HOSTEXEC-class additions to the server surface.
value_conditions.kind: CLI/config list of experimental tool or group names

value_conditions.effect: Adds 'find_examples' to the enabled experimental set; `find_examples` is already in STABLE_TOOLS so this does not change its exposure.
Redirects `find_examples` to a runtime example database built from that directory (`setupRuntimeExamples`), bypassing workspace discovery and the bundled database.
`find_examples` is not registered at all (logger warning, returns false), removing its SECRET reach.

value_conditions.default: falls back to process.cwd() when the client advertises no roots
value_conditions.effect: Restricts filesystem reach: `createRootRestrictedHost` roots are set from the client roots and `list_projects`/`resolveWorkspaceAndProject` limit scanning to those roots; without the capability the server falls back to `process.cwd()`.
